headline: KSE-100 rebounded off Friday's lows to close only −0.42% (171,021) — drawdown from peak pulls back to ~9.8%, just under the 10% correction line, not clearly through it as Friday's intraday read suggested; Brent oil plunged >4% on a Pakistan-brokered US-Iran talks report, a genuine de-escalation signal; portfolio ~+1.1%, no holding moved >5%; AVN dropped straight through its own Rs 32-33 sell zone to Rs 31.33 (8th straight review) — sell half at market Monday, don't wait longer; SBP MPC Monday Jul 27 (2 days out, hold expected); EFERT H1 results Wed Jul 29 (4 days out)
market: The KSE-100 closed Friday Jul 24 at 171,021.20, down 718.24 points (−0.42%) — a third straight losing session, but a far milder finish than the morning suggested: the index fell as low as 169,512.88 before Friday-prayer trading paused, then rallied to an intraday high of 172,718.66 by 2:30pm before late-session profit-taking pulled it back down. Against the Jan 23, 2026 all-time high of 189,556, Friday's actual close puts the drawdown at ~9.78% — just under the 10% line the standing plan uses to trigger dry-powder deployment, milder than the 10.1-10.6% estimated off Friday's intraday prices in yesterday's review. The bigger story: Brent crude fell over 4% Friday to ~$96.18/bbl on a Reuters report that Pakistan, backed by China, is pushing to restart US-Iran talks — real de-escalation after weeks of an oil-driven selloff, and likely why the index found a floor instead of continuing to slide. SBP's first FY27 MPC meeting is now just 2 days out (Monday Jul 27); a Topline Securities poll has 97% of analysts expecting the policy rate held at 11.5% given the still-elevated (if now falling) oil backdrop. No fresh IMF news. Your portfolio, marked to Friday's close: ~Rs 9.60M value on ~Rs 9.50M invested (+1.1% unrealized, down slightly from +1.6% Thursday) — broad, shallow moves across nearly every line, none beyond about 2%, consistent with the muted index close; no holding moved more than 3% day-over-day. AVN kept sliding to Rs 31.33 (from Rs 32.06 Thursday, a further −2.1%) with still no PSX filing addressing the FY25 earnings collapse — this is now the eighth straight review flagging it, and the price has now dropped straight through the Rs 32-33 sell zone without a single bounce (Rs 34.24 → 33.11 → 32.82 → 32.67 → 32.06 → 31.33). EFERT's board still meets Wed Jul 29, 2026, 9am for H1 results/dividend — now 4 days away, still outside the 3-day notification window. CPHL's REIT demerger remains exactly where it was Jul 8 (board-approved transfer of two Lahore properties into the Citi Core Holdings SPV for 331.72M shares; awaiting the next regulatory/shareholder step) — checked again, no movement. No ex-dividend dates found within the next 3 days for any holding (MEBL's next ex-div isn't expected until around August).

actions.title: Avanceon — fundamentals broken, price still sliding, not bouncing
actions.detail: Your largest stock position (Rs 800K in) and worst performer (−30.5%, now at Rs 31.33 vs Rs 32.06 last review — a further slide, no bounce). FY25 net income fell ~68%, Q3 revenue fell 44%, margins collapsed from 12% to 4%, 3-year shareholder return −32%. Eight straight reviews have now flagged this and the stock has dropped straight through the old Rs 32-33 sell zone without a single up day — Rs 34.24 → 33.11 → 32.82 → 32.67 → 32.06 → 31.33 — with no company-specific news to explain any of it. Waiting for a better exit price has just cost more than it's saved. Sell half at market Monday regardless of where it opens. No catalyst expected before the Sep 2, 2026 earnings report; exit the rest fully if that report shows no recovery.

notes: Big picture for a 10–25 year horizon: (1) Your only real problem is AVN — a large position with deteriorating fundamentals that's now eight reviews overdue for actually selling, and the price has now dropped straight through the sell zone while you wait; fix that first, Monday. (2) The KSE-100's drawdown from its Jan 23, 2026 peak (189,556) is a photo finish around the 10% correction line — 9.4-10.6% on Thursday/Friday intraday, ~9.8% at Friday's actual close — with Friday's >4% oil plunge on a Pakistan-brokered US-Iran de-escalation report a genuine positive sign. (4) Reinvest all dividends. (5) Expect 10–15% drawdowns like this one; they are the price of the 40%+ years — don't panic-sell the core holdings, just deploy the dry powder as planned. (6) Dust positions UPFL (~Rs 76K, illiquid but fine to hold) and AIAIP/AKDISIF (fund dust, ~Rs 2,500 combined) remain flagged for consolidation whenever you next transact — not urgent. (7) Mark Jul 29, 2026 as the date to actually check EFERT's H1 results — it's a confirmed board-meeting date, now 4 days out; will alert once inside the 3-day window.
